name: FVAPPS (Formally Verified Automated Programming Progress Standards)
description: We introduce the Formally Verified Automated Programming Progress Standards, or FVAPPS, a benchmark of 4715 samples for writing programs and proving their correctness, the largest formal verification benchmark, including 1083 curated and quality controlled samples. Previously, APPS provided a benchmark and dataset for programming puzzles to be completed in Python and checked against unit tests, of the kind seen in technical assessments in the software engineering industry. Building upon recent approaches for benchmarks in interactive theorem proving, we generalize the unit tests to Lean 4 theorems given without proof (i.e., using Lean's "sorry" keyword). On the 406 theorems of 100 randomly selected samples, Sonnet correctly proves 30% and Gemini correctly proves 18%. We challenge the machine learning and program synthesis communities to solve both each general purpose programming problem and its associated correctness specifications. The benchmark is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/quinn-dougherty/fvapps.
evaluation_method: automated proof verification (task_success_rate: percentage of programs/theorems that verify in Lean 4)
general_score_metric: task_success_rate (percentage of samples with verified proofs/programs)
typical_sota_score: approximately 18–30% on reported subsets (varies by model and subset)
reputation: A notable and ambitious benchmark in the ML + formal methods community — the largest formal verification dataset to date — attracting attention from researchers working on proof synthesis and verified programming.
notes: Requires Lean 4 environment and proof checking rather than simple unit tests; susceptible to training-data contamination (models pre-trained on Lean/related corpora), computationally heavy to evaluate, and verification can be brittle to small proof-format differences.
